title: Prove the sharp six-line rational anchor-box floor
body:
The first open line-count case in PR3031 is settled: for rational six-row, three-column factors with nonzero diagonal and canonical `tau_i>=1`, the ordered anchor box keeps at least four lines. The bound is sharp. Restriction with the original normalization also gives the requested floor four at seven lines.

`research/fstar-six-line-floor/PROOF.md` is an analytic proof, with no finite-search premise. Unit-label graph arguments handle zero, one and two singleton tied sets; the remaining configurations use primitive-row proportionality and exact annihilator dimensions. The three-singleton case explicitly respects the directed witness order.

Evidence:

- Duplicating each line of Aaron Wang's PR2978 core gives `M=diag(8 J2,8 J2,12 J2)`, rank three, `tau=2` on every line, and box exactly four. The upper bound is a triangular-rank obstruction.
- A separately written target-first Gaussian box oracle checks the exact fixture and source-definition agreement against authenticated PR2914 bytes. Its affine solver is checked against 20,136 direct truth-table systems.
- Controls cover wrong forward order, parity-preserving out-of-anchor labels, `tau=0`, zero diagonal, rank removal, signed rational rescaling and counterfeit source rejection before execution.
- An exact rational duplicate-blocker fixture has different even rows choosing different physical copies of the same blocker type and nonproportional target rows. The proof handles that case by a 2+2 witness or rank-four contradiction; the control also rejects the wrong even-pair order.
- Python 3.12.15 registered normal and isolated optimized replays pass; metadata/source pins, frozen Git byte comparisons, and publication-byte/source-history checks pass.

This is a scoped rational box theorem, not formal verification of the full F-star conjecture, a native/controller/supplier result, or a new kappa. The selected frontier is unchanged. The next threshold question is five kept lines at `v=8`.

Credit: Aaron Wang/navinor for the box/valuation lineage and three-line core; DreamingOfClouds for F-star/certificate origins; Arham Tahir for the earlier joint triple classification. Full attribution and exact source exports are retained in the package. New work by Sagar Thakrar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate proof/checker review runs; no independent human review claimed.

Canonical claim and handoff: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-19008465. Original card `independent-moment`, explicitly changed scope following the PR3031/PR3332 open question. Based on refreshed canonical main `6f100d4bb5083f8c35d96fd95a539811c62f245c`; fork synced and branch rebased before publication.
